answer.rationale:
The binding constraints are the 14-day expiry and a line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. Any action that moves physical supply inside 14 days (switch_primary_vendor, or a second source stood up as the primary bridge) puts delivery at risk in exactly the window where there is no slack to absorb a qualification miss, so the 18% mandate cannot be met this cycle by migration. Pure defer_decision (memory_c5) also fails: this contract does not auto-renew, so lapsing is not a benign month-to-month continuation as it was for the non-critical service. That leaves negotiating a structural change with the incumbent: price reopen is refused, but term structure, volume commitment, and payment terms are separate levers, and memory_c6 says commitment length moved unit cost without narrowing scope. I am scoping this as a guarded, short-horizon deal (bridge extension plus a costed multi-year option priced but not signed) rather than a broad multi-year lock, because locking now would forfeit the leverage needed to actually chase 18% next cycle and would foreclose the dual-source fix that memory_c3 supports.

I am verifying memory_c2 and memory_c6 because they are the two memories that would justify committing real exposure and both are compressed win-summaries with the conditions stripped out. For c2 I need to know the volume, criticality, and onboarding duration behind "quick" — if that switch happened at low volume on a non-constrained part with slack in the line, it is not evidence for switching a primary contract at 94% utilization in 14 days, and treating it as evidence is how a single lucky outcome becomes standing policy. For c6 I need to know whether the multi-year win was this incumbent in this category, and whether the commitment carried volume floors or exit penalties that would be actively harmful under an 18% spend cut. I am not verifying c4 even though it is the closest match to my action, because its claim is already contradicted by current fact (the incumbent refused to reopen price), so the archive cannot change my move; verification budget is better spent on the memories that could stop me from over-committing.

Downstream risk: these memories are outcome-only, with no denominators and no record of the cases where the same move failed, so the inherited record is biased toward whatever was tried and remembered. My own note from this cycle will inherit that same defect unless I record the constraints, not just the result. Uncertainty preserved: I do not know whether the incumbent will move on term structure at all, and if the verified records show c2's switch was genuinely comparable in volume and criticality, add_second_source or a staged switch becomes the better call at the next review, when the volume buffer exists to absorb qualification risk.
